newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindustan Lever slumps 3.4 pct in Delhi.
newsitem.headline: Hindustan Lever slumps 3.4 pct in Delhi.

text.p: Shares of food-to-detergent conglomerate Hindustan Lever Ltd (HLL) fell 46.50 rupees on the Delhi bourse on Friday to close at 1,318.50, brokers said.
One analyst said the stock was due for a technical correction that could have been triggered by a dispute between the company and distributors of its products in the southern state of Kerala.
"HLL has been rising three to four percent each day all week, and a fall of less than five percent is largely a correction," an analyst at SocGen Crosby Securities said.
He said one factor that could have triggered the selloff was a row between the company and distributors in Kerala.
The distributors, which are demanding higher margins, have banned HLL's products from the state.
Traders said that the steep drop in Hindustan Lever shares helped to drag the Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index down 0.75 point to 860.36.
Unilever Plc is the largest shareholder in HLL with a 47.7 percent stake, and was recently granted permission to raise its holding to 51 percent.
